sections.heading: Set Up a Recoverable First Run

blocks.title: Check the content warning first
blocks.text: The game includes jumpscares, loud sounds, flashing and disturbing images, blood, cartoon gore, violence, drug use, obsessive behavior, toxic relationships, and crude language. Lower volume and choose a suitable environment before continuing.

blocks.alt: Dialogue and bell-menu controls in Helping Your Boyfriend
blocks.caption: Dialogue and bell-menu controls in Helping Your Boyfriend

blocks.text: Version 1.0.1 includes gameplay difficulty choices. Pick the level that lets you recognize and act on prompts without turning the sequence into an accessibility barrier. A lower setting does not remove the point of the story; it changes the execution pressure around the interactive moments.

items.title: Confirm your input device
items.text: Use a mouse and a keyboard with dedicated arrow keys if possible. Compact keyboards may require a function layer that is too slow for directional prompts.

items.title: Open the bell menu
items.text: Click the bell at the top of the game and confirm that Save, Load, and Settings are reachable before a minigame starts.

items.title: Create two save lanes
items.text: Keep one story checkpoint before a major relationship branch and one mechanical checkpoint immediately before an interactive sequence.

sections.heading: Control Dialogue and the Bell Menu

blocks.text: Left click or Enter advances a line and confirms a visible choice. Space hides or restores the dialogue box, which is useful when a character or object is partly covered. Press L to open the history log and reread a line you advanced too quickly. Press A for auto-play only when the timing is comfortable; turn it off before a choice, sudden warning, or minigame transition.

Holding Ctrl or pressing Tab skips text, but skip mode can carry momentum into a new prompt. Release the key whenever the background changes, a clickable object appears, or the story returns to a choice you have not seen. The history log recovers dialogue, not necessarily a missed physical interaction, so a nearby save remains essential.

Move the pointer to the middle of the object the game expects you to manipulate. Press and hold the primary mouse button, move in one continuous motion, and release only after the object itself—not just the cursor—crosses into the receiving area. If the destination does not react, return to the original position and start closer to the object's center.

Browser scaling can make an illustrated target and its active hit area appear misaligned. Keep system display scaling stable, use the game's intended window size, and avoid changing zoom during the task. On touch devices, begin away from system gesture edges and keep contact until the target acknowledges the drop. Do not repeatedly tap after a failed drag, because that can select or advance something else.

items.title: Acquire
items.text: Hold on the movable object until its position or cursor state changes.

items.title: Carry
items.text: Move steadily while keeping the button or touch contact down.

items.title: Confirm
items.text: Wait for target feedback before releasing or starting another action.

items.title: Reset
items.text: If nothing changed, reload the mechanical checkpoint rather than replaying the whole chapter.

sections.heading: Prepare for Arrow-Key and Space QTEs

blocks.text: Quick-time events use the arrow keys plus Space. Put one hand over the four arrows and the other thumb over Space before the first prompt. Watch the current symbol and press once; do not enter a sequence remembered from another attempt, because the prompt order may change or your earlier failure may have shifted the timing.

blocks.alt: A drag interaction with its target area
blocks.caption: A drag interaction with its target area

blocks.text: If the QTE repeatedly fails, lower the gameplay difficulty, confirm that Num Lock or a function layer is not remapping the arrow cluster, and close software that captures Space or directional keys. A 60-percent keyboard without dedicated arrows is a genuine hardware limitation for this release because no remapping control has been confirmed. An external keyboard is more reliable than trying to toggle layers under time pressure.

blocks.title: Separate reaction failure from route failure
blocks.text: If the story continues after a missed prompt, read the next scene before reloading. The failed QTE may be a valid branch. Reload only when you want to test the successful result or the interface stopped responding.

sections.heading: Save, Skip, and Recover Without Losing the Route

blocks.text: Name saves by purpose: before first QTE, before room search, before late relationship choice. Avoid filling every slot with nearly identical autosaves. When a route goes wrong, return to the closest checkpoint that controls the cause: use the mechanical save for a missed prompt and the story save for an approval or investigation decision.

blocks.alt: A directional quick-time prompt and response state
blocks.caption: A directional quick-time prompt and response state

blocks.text: If the game seems paused, check whether auto-play is waiting, the dialogue box is hidden, or the window lost focus. Press Space once to restore the box, click inside the game, and open the history log to confirm the last completed line. If controls still do nothing, use Load from the bell menu. Restarting the application is the final step, not the first.

items: Do not hold Ctrl while a new scene is loading.
Do not overwrite the only save made before a branching choice.
Do not interpret missing audio as failed input when the image advanced.
Do not force a QTE on inaccessible hardware when the difficulty option can reduce the demand.

blocks.text: Windows, macOS, and Android are official platforms, but the complete touch equivalent for every keyboard-style prompt has not been confirmed across devices. Follow the prompt shown by your build. If a touch QTE is uncomfortable or unclear, use the difficulty setting or move the save to a supported desktop setup when possible rather than guessing that every arrow key has an invisible swipe equivalent.

On desktop, security warnings can appear for newly downloaded independent games. Obtain the file from the official creator page, scan it with your normal security tools, and make your own decision; do not disable system protection globally. On macOS, application permission prompts belong to the operating system and should be handled through its normal privacy controls, not by downloading an unknown replacement.

faq.question: What are all the confirmed Helping Your Boyfriend controls?
faq.answer: Left click or Enter advances and chooses; the mouse points and drags; Space hides the dialogue box; L opens history; A toggles auto-play; Ctrl or Tab skips; arrows plus Space handle QTEs; the bell opens Save, Load, and Settings.

faq.question: Can I remap the arrow-key QTE?
faq.answer: A remapping option has not been confirmed in version 1.0.1. Use a keyboard with dedicated arrows or lower the gameplay difficulty if a compact layout makes the sequence inaccessible.

faq.question: Why did my drag not register?
faq.answer: Start from the object's center, hold continuously, move the object itself into the active target, and release after visual feedback. Keep zoom stable.

faq.question: Should I reload every failed minigame?
faq.answer: No. Read the next scene first. Some failures can lead into a valid route; reload when testing another result or when the interface actually stopped.

guides.title: Helping Your Boyfriend Endings Walkthrough
guides.summary: Plan four controlled runs with reusable saves, relationship targets, pills, investigation clues, and the late key-and-room branch clearly marked for spoilers.
guides.introduction: This version 1.0.1 walkthrough reveals route requirements for all four endings. Finish one blind run first, then use the checkpoints and decision paths below.

image.alt: A spoiler-safe checkpoint branching toward four sealed route folders

seo.title: Helping Your Boyfriend Endings Walkthrough Guide
seo.description: Reach all four Helping Your Boyfriend endings with version 1.0.1 relationship targets, pill choices, clue checkpoints, the key route, and recovery steps.

blocks.title: Full route spoilers begin here
blocks.text: The steps below identify relationship direction, pill choices, investigation requirements, and late actions for every ending. Complete a blind run first if you want the story's reversals unprompted.

blocks.alt: Save and load slots arranged before a route split
blocks.caption: Save and load slots arranged before a route split

blocks.text: The four named endings are separate from earlier game-over states. Surviving the minigames is required to continue far enough to reach them. The route then depends on Adrian affection, Ian affection, the pill decisions, and—for the later investigation paths—whether you preserved the phone number, found the address, and opened the locked room with the key.

Think of the structure as two broad families. Endings 1 and 2 use high Adrian affection and low Ian affection, then split around the pills and a late violent option. Endings 3 and 4 use low Adrian affection plus the complete investigation sequence; Ian affection separates those two. This model is easier to reproduce than memorizing isolated dialogue buttons.

items.title: Checkpoint A: before relationship choices accumulate
items.text: Use this to build a high-Adrian/low-Ian run or a low-Adrian route without replaying customization and opening scenes.

items.title: Checkpoint B: before the pill sequence
items.text: Preserve the established affection state, then compare taking Ian's pill, taking Adrian's pill, or refusing as the target route requires.

items.title: Checkpoint C: before the late body-and-key decision
items.text: Use this only after recording the phone number and room address on an investigation route. It allows you to retry the key and locked-room steps without rebuilding affection.

blocks.text: Do not overwrite Checkpoint A after moving into a low-Adrian route. The key option depends on Adrian affection being low enough; a save made after the requirement has already failed cannot repair it. Similarly, remembering the phone number yourself is not enough if the protagonist did not annotate it in the game state.

items.title: Build high Adrian affection
items.text: Choose responses that support Adrian and keep his approval high through the relationship sections.

items.title: Keep Ian affection low
items.text: Avoid building a supportive Ian relationship on this run.

items.title: Refuse Ian's pill
items.text: When Ian offers the pill, do not take it.

items.title: Take Adrian's pill
items.text: Accept Adrian's pill later in the route.

items.title: Do not use the scalpel on Adrian
items.text: When the late violent choice appears, leave the scalpel unused.

blocks.text: If this route produces Ending 2 instead, the affection pattern is probably correct but one of the pill decisions was reversed. Reload Checkpoint B rather than rebuilding the entire relationship. If the route ends in a game over before those choices, repair the failed minigame first.

items.title: Retain high Adrian affection
items.text: Use the same supportive Adrian pattern as Ending 1.

items.title: Keep Ian affection low
items.text: Do not raise Ian approval enough to enter his later branch.

items.title: Take Ian's pill
items.text: Accept the pill from Ian during his sequence.

items.title: Refuse Adrian's pill
items.text: Do not take Adrian's later pill.

blocks.text: Ending 2 is the cleanest pill comparison with Ending 1. Use the same Checkpoint A route and branch at Checkpoint B. If changing those choices does not alter the result, recheck whether Ian affection accidentally rose during an earlier conversation.

sections.heading: Prepare the Investigation for Endings 3 and 4

items.title: Lower Adrian affection
items.text: Choose disapproving or resistant responses consistently enough that the late key option becomes available.

items.title: Record the number
items.text: During the relevant scene, have the protagonist annotate the phone number shown on their arm.

items.title: Find the address
items.text: Inspect Adrian's room and preserve the address discovered there.

items.title: Take Ian's pill
items.text: Accept Ian's pill on both investigation endings.

items.title: Refuse Adrian's pill
items.text: Decline Adrian's later pill on both investigation endings.

items.title: Take the key and enter the locked room
items.text: After the confrontation, take the key from Adrian's body, open the locked room, and do this before going outside.

blocks.alt: An investigation clue state used by later endings
blocks.caption: An investigation clue state used by later endings

blocks.title: The key is a state check
blocks.text: If the key option does not appear, Adrian affection is not low enough. Loading immediately before the body will not fix the relationship value; return to Checkpoint A and make the low-affection pattern clearer.

For Ending 3, keep both Adrian affection and Ian affection low. Complete the number and address investigation, take Ian's pill, refuse Adrian's pill, take the key, and visit the locked room before going outside. Low affection with both men distinguishes this route from Ending 4.

If you completed the room sequence but reached Ending 4, the investigation worked and Ian affection is too high for Ending 3. Reload from the relationship checkpoint and choose more distant Ian responses while preserving every clue and pill requirement.

For Ending 4, keep Adrian affection low and build Ian affection high. As with Ending 3, annotate the phone number, locate the address in Adrian's room, take Ian's pill, refuse Adrian's pill, take the key, and enter the locked room before leaving the house.

If the locked room sequence completes but Ending 3 appears, raise Ian affection earlier without softening the low-Adrian pattern. If neither investigation ending appears, verify the phone number and address were recorded by the protagonist and that the room was entered before going outside.

rows: Reload the mechanical checkpoint or reduce difficulty
Pill decisions stayed on the Ending 1 pattern
Use Checkpoint B and take Ian's pill while refusing Adrian's
Return to Checkpoint A and choose a clearer low-Adrian pattern
Raise Ian affection while keeping the investigation state
Lower Ian affection without losing the clues

Repeat the full investigation checklist before going outside

blocks.alt: A late route confirmation screen with outcome details withheld
blocks.caption: A late route confirmation screen with outcome details withheld

blocks.text: Change the smallest state that explains the mismatch. Rebuilding every choice after each miss makes it harder to know which condition worked. Keep ending-confirmation saves separate so you can compare the final screen without overwriting route checkpoints.

items: Ending 1: high Adrian, low Ian, refuse Ian pill, take Adrian pill, do not use the scalpel.
Ending 2: high Adrian, low Ian, take Ian pill, refuse Adrian pill.
Ending 3: low Adrian, low Ian, complete number/address/key/locked-room investigation, take Ian pill, refuse Adrian pill.
Ending 4: low Adrian, high Ian, complete the same investigation, take Ian pill, refuse Adrian pill.
Keep game-over states separate from the four ending count.

blocks.text: After all four ending confirmations, keep one save from each relationship family rather than every intermediate attempt. That leaves a compact archive for replaying favorite scenes or checking a future version without confusing old and new route state.

faq.question: How many endings are in Helping Your Boyfriend?
faq.answer: There are four route endings, separate from earlier game-over states. You must survive the minigames to continue to those endings.

faq.question: Why can I not take the key?
faq.answer: The option requires Adrian affection to be low enough. Return to an earlier relationship checkpoint and choose a more consistently resistant pattern.

faq.question: What separates Ending 3 and Ending 4?
faq.answer: Both use low Adrian affection and the complete investigation path. Ian affection is low for Ending 3 and high for Ending 4.

faq.question: Do I need both the phone number and address?
faq.answer: Yes for the investigation endings. Have the protagonist annotate the number and inspect Adrian's room for the address, then use the key and locked room before leaving.
